name: UV-protective sunglasses
lead: UV-protective sunglasses have lenses that block ultraviolet radiation, ideally labeled UV400 or 99 to 100 percent UVA and UVB. Larger or wraparound frames cover more of the surrounding skin.
They protect the eyes and the thin periocular skin and reduce squinting.

paras: Lens materials and coatings absorb UV before it reaches the eye, and frames shade the eyelids. Tint darkness does not indicate UV blocking. I did not find systematic reviews specific to sunglasses and wrinkles; the evidence comes from dermatology and ophthalmology guidance, and eyelid skin cancers are common sun-related tumors.

Poor-quality lenses can have dark tint but little UV blocking, which dilates the pupil and increases exposure. Sunglasses do not protect all the periocular skin, so sunscreen is still needed. The claim that sunglasses prevent crow's feet is plausible through less squinting but untested here.

studies.title: How to select the perfect pair of sunglasses (Skin Cancer Foundation guidance)
